The Hurricanes should have their star receiver back in time for the postseason if the recovery goes according to plan

        No. 1 Miami may be without star receiver Malachi Toney against No. 11 Notre Dame on Saturday, but the team hopes to have him back in time for the postseason. Sources tell CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz that the early feel on a return timetable is that Toney is expected to miss four to six weeks after undergoing ankle surgery.Toney suffered a high-ankle sprain in practice this week that will knock him out for the rest of the regular season, but the team hopes surgery will help the sophomore receiver return in time to chase a national championship.Based on that timeline, the Hurricanes could get Toney back in time for the ACC Championship Game. Depending on how the rest of the Canes' regular season plays out, they may not even need to risk playing him in that game.If the Hurricanes can pull out a win over the Fighting Irish on Saturday night, it's hard to see them slipping up in the regular season. Their final three games are against Duke, Virginia Tech and Boston College, all of which are at home. At this point, the conference title game may be more risk than reward for Toney and Miami.
Even if Toney's recovery winds up taking closer to six weeks, that's plenty of time for him to be healthy for the College Football Playoff. The first round doesn't kick off until Dec. 18, and if Miami earns a top-four seed and first-round bye, it wouldn't play until Dec. 30 at the earliest.Prior to his injury, Toney was building a strong case for the Heisman Trophy as he leads the ACC in receptions (73), receiving yards (1,027) and receiving touchdowns (13). With Toney out of the lineup, Miami will need someone else to step up and replace his production with Duke transfer Cooper Barkate being the most obvious candidate.It also helps that Miami has another Heisman candidate leading its offense at quarterback, Darian Mensah. Facing Notre Dame's defense on the road may be the toughest test Mensah has gotten all season, but he's made it look easy to this point, throwing for 25 touchdowns and just one interception.
Although the loss of Toney puts a damper on tonight's matchup, it remains one of the biggest games of the season. The Hurricanes need as much wiggle room as they can get with Toney set to miss the month of November, and the Fighting Irish clearly need a signature win after the initial College Football Playoff Rankings placed them at No. 11.

Although this isn't a great free agent class, there are dozens of quality players available. You just have to know where to look

        The 2026-27 MLB offseason is a little more than a week old now and we're still waiting for the first big trade or free agent signing. That isn't unusual, though. The hot stove, like the regular season, is a marathon, not a sprint. A lockout is expected when the collective bargaining agreement ends at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1, and there should be a flurry of activity before then. We ranked the offseason's top 50 free agents, and although it is not a great class, there are dozens of quality players available. You just have to know where to look. Here now are five players who did not rank among our top 50 free agents, but would nonetheless be good options and solid pickups for teams that want to raise their floor and improve their supporting cast.  RHP Bryan Abreu 
It was a tale of two seasons for the 29-year-old Bryan Abreu, who had a 5.81 ERA before the All-Star break and a 1.71 ERA after. The under-the-hood estimators, like FIP and xERA, were better in the second half as well, though Abreu lost close to 2 mph off his fastball this year and, not coincidentally, a whole bunch of swings and misses. Abreu is third in appearances and second in innings among relievers since 2022 and it's possible the workload is catching up to him. There's still enough bat-missing ability and late-inning experience here for Abreu to contribute to a contender's bullpen. It just might happen as a seventh-inning guy moving forward, not as the Moment of Truth™ reliever who pitches in the game's biggest moments.  IF J.P. Crawford 
If you're looking for a bottom of the order guy who will take walks and give you 10-15 home runs, that's J.P. Crawford. His defense, specifically his range and arm, has slipped so much in his early 30s that he's no longer a viable shortstop, though he played 33 games at third base this past season. I like him better at second base, but third base works too. Crawford gets on-base at a decent clip and won't strike out excessively, plus he's long been regarded as an excellent teammate and grade-A clubhouse guy. It seems like his time with the Mariners is over and it's for the best. Crawford can go elsewhere, play a new position, and just be part of the lineup rather than one of the faces of the franchise. 

        
            
                Ranking the top 50 MLB free agents for the 2026-27 offseason, plus landing spots for every player
                
                    Mike Axisa                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
 LHP Sean Newcomb 
Due to injury and ineffectiveness, it looked like Sean Newcomb was on his way out of baseball two years ago. He then reinvented himself as a sinker/curveball guy and carved out a nice second phase to his career as a workhorse utility reliever who won't beat himself with walks (an early career bugaboo) and will limit hard contact in the air. Newcomb, 33, worked at least 90 innings the last two seasons while pitching in every possible role. He closed out games, worked high leverage as a setup guy, soaked up innings in long relief, and opened a few times as well. Newcomb is likely miscast as a go-to bullpen option, though he can be a valuable third or fourth option for a contender. The utility reliever is all the rage these days and Newcomb fits the profile to a T.  RHP Emilio Pagán 
Now 35, Emilio Pagán was sensational after returning from a hamstring injury in July, pitching to a 1.88 ERA with 34 strikeouts and only five walks in his final 28 ⅔ innings. The downside is the same as it's always been: Pagán is exceptionally home run prone (career 1.51 HR/9), which is a bad trait for a late-inning reliever who pitches almost exclusively in close games. His fastball remains firm, though, and his splitter is an elite swing-and-miss pitch that allows him to neutralize righties and lefties. As long as you're willing to live with the home run risk, Pagán remains a capable high-leverage reliever, one who is not out of place pitching important innings for a contending team. 

        
            
                Top 25 MLB trade candidates for 2026-27 offseason: Paul Skenes, Jeremy Peña and more who could move
                
                    Dayn Perry                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
 DH Joc Pederson 
Platoon DHs are not the hottest commodity, but Joc Pederson fills the role about as well as anyone in the game. He's a left-handed hitter, so he's on the heavy side of the platoon, and he authored a .245/.338/.496 line with terrific ball-tracking data (exit velocity, etc.) against righties. If you must play him in the field, Pederson can stand in right field or at first base for about six innings before being subbed out for a defensive replacement. He's essentially a bat-only player, though. Pederson will turn 35 in April and he's still a powerful and productive hitter against righties and an elite clubhouse vibes dude.

        One of the best modern-day rivalries in college football headlines on Saturday when No. 5 Alabama and No. 14 LSU meet in Baton Rouge for the 91st meeting in the series. The Crimson Tide hold a 58-27-5 advantage overall, but it's the 13-2 record in the past 15 meetings that has given them the upper hand in a battle between programs that would otherwise be considered peers. This is, after all, set to be the 25th time that both schools are inside the top 15 of the AP Top 25 poll and with Alabama's recent crowning as a top-five team in the College Football Playoff rankings, there's even more ranked-on-ranked intrigue. LSU is hoping that the home field advantage of Death Valley can play a role in the game, as the Tigers are 32-3 in their last 35 home games in Tiger Stadium. Speaking of streaks, the game also presents LSU coach Lane Kiffin with a chance to finally defeat Alabama as a head coach. The former Crimson Tide offensive coordinator lost to Nick Saban once as Tennessee's head coach in 2009, then four times between 2020-23 as Ole Miss' head coach, when they were SEC West division rivals. That 0-5 record against the Crimson Tide, paired with LSU's recent struggles in the series, provides plenty of extra motivation for the home team looking to roar back into the playoff race.   Alabama vs. LSU: Need to know  Alabama's injury report will be an X-factor: There will be key updates throughout the week, perhaps all the way up to warm-ups, that will determine the health of the Crimson Tide and their ability to perform to the expectations of their top-five rating. Starting center Racin Delgatty has missed multiple games while dealing with injury, and his absence has been noticeable on an offensive line that has cooled off since putting up 49+ points in consecutive wins against Florida State, South Carolina and Mississippi State. The Crimson Tide have failed to record 70+ rushing yards as a team in each of their last two games and allowed 21 sacks in SEC play, which ranks 14th among 16 teams in the league. Alabama will also be looking for updates from star wide receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams and cornerback Zabien Brown, adding to the unknowns for how the Tide will stack up against LSU. LSU passing attack rounding into form: No one in the SEC had a more productive passing attack in the month of October than LSU, which averaged 339.5 passing yards across all four games last month. The Tigers went 3-1 across those games, only losing to top-10 Kentucky by one point in Lexington on a walk-off two-point try. LSU now leads the SEC and ranks tied for 7th nationally on the season, averaging 318.0 passing yards per game, and the improvements have come with both Sam Leavitt's improved play and the emergence of Jackson Harris as a go-to receiver. A transfer from Hawaii, Harris played three whole games before scoring his first touchdown of the season but has exploded ever since with seven touchdown catches across the last five games. That includes four multiple-touchdown games and a yards-per-reception average (17.6) that ranks 4th among all SEC pass catchers. 
Kalen DeBoer set up in some favorable situational spots: When Alabama hired Kalen DeBoer away from Washington to take over in Tuscaloosa after Nick Saban's retirement, his track record as a big-time, high-leverage coach met the demands of the job. Since Alabama is almost always playing in high-pressure games against quality opponents, the school needed to know that Saban's successor would be ready for those moments. Currently, DeBoer is 21-8 against AP-ranked teams as a head coach, which is the fourth-best record in AP poll history with a minimum of 20 games coached (.724 winning percentage). His company on that list, for those unaware, is one spot behind Urban Meyer (.746) and one spot ahead of Kirby Smart (.710). DeBoer has also won eight straight games after a bye, with the last defeat in this spot coming in 2020 as the head coach of Fresno State.  Where to watch Alabama vs. LSU live  Date: Saturday, Nov. 7 | Time: 3:30 p.m. ET  Location: Tiger Stadium -- Baton Rouge, Louisiana  TV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free)  Alabama vs. LSU prediction, picks  While the combination of LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt and Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell provides the potential for plenty of points, this game could end up being decided by both defenses. Alabama's offensive injuries have clearly limited their ability to execute on schedule, and LSU's defense represents the best test they've faced since the loss at Tennessee. In the same manner, LSU's pass attack could set them up for some of the turnovers that have powered Alabama's excellence this season (+7 turnover margin is tied for 11th nationally) and prevent touchdowns even after successful drives. All in all, it points to a lower-scoring classic, where I'll favor the home team to make big plays late. Pick: Under 52.5

title: Inside the numbers: Why Luka Dončić is runaway MVP frontrunner so far this NBA season - CBS Sports
description: Dončić scored 53 points in a Lakers win over the Blazers Friday night and looks like the runaway MVP in the early
body:
Dončić scored 53 points in a Lakers win over the Blazers Friday night and looks like the runaway MVP in the early going
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:25 am ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Luka Doncic delivered another casual masterpiece with 53 points in a 124-118 Lakers victory over the Trail Blazers on Friday night. He outscored Portland by himself 20-15 in the third quarter. He dropped a three-quarter-court buzzer-beater to end the first half. He added five rebounds and five assists for fun. And the Lakers are now atop the Western Conference standings at 8-2.If the season were to end today, Dončić would be the runaway MVP, maybe joining 2015-16 Stephen Curry as the second unanimous winner in NBA history. His box scores will always be somewhat skewed given his usage, but that context notwithstanding, these numbers are downright stupid. 
Let's dive a little deeper into the numbers behind Dončić's historic start. 3Dončić has become the third player in Lakers history to score at least 35 points in seven straight games, joining Kobe Bryant and Elgin Baylor. 4Dončić is just the fourth Lakers player to put up four straight 40-point games, joining Bryant, Baylor and George Mikan. You'll notice names like LeBron James, Shaquille O'Neal, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar and Magic Johnson missing from these lists. Some franchise marks are oversold. Not when it comes to the Lakers. 
5Dončić has made at least five 3-pointers in seven straight games. If he continues that streak for another five games, he will break James Harden's NBA record of 12 straight. 6Dončić is currently averaging six made 3-pointers per game. He has played in nine of the Lakers' 10 games. Meaning, if he stays on this pace of six 3s per game while playing in 90% of L.A.'s games, he would end up making 426 3s, which would break Curry's single-season record of 402. Staying on six, Dončić also owns the non-Wilt Chamberlain NBA record with six 40-point games in his team's first 10 games. 
7Dončić has now logged seven straight games with at least 35 points, five assists and five rebounds, tying Oscar Robertson for the longest such streak in history. 13.7Dončić is currently attempting 13.7 3-pointers per game. If that volume holds up, it would break Harden's NBA record of 13.2 attempts per game in 2018-19. But Harden only made 36.8% of his 3s that year. Dončić, as you'll see shortly, is blowing that number out of the water. 
16With two 50-point games so far and just 11% of the schedule completed, Dončić is currently on pace to cook up 16 50-burgers this season, which would shatter Bryant's non-Chamberlain record of 10 in a single season. Chamberlain, for the record, had 45 50-point games in 1961-62, which is just absurd. 
40.1After Friday's performance, Dončić is now averaging 40.1 points per game. The only other player in history to average 40 through the first nine games of a season is Chamberlain, who is basically a category unto himself in these statistical side-by-sides. The most Michael Jordan ever averaged through the first nine games of a season was 38.6 in 1986-87. 41.9Dončić is shooting 41.9% from 3 to start the year. That isn't likely to continue. Like Harden, he's been a volume marksman to this point as a career 35% 3-point shooter. But right now he is absolutely dialed, particularly with his step-back, which, according to NBA.com shot tracking, he entered Friday night knocking down at a Curry-like 43% clip. 
Dončić is reading the game on autopilot at this point in his career. If you double him, he's zipping the right pass. If you single cover him, he's either powering his way into the paint or, more often, getting right into this step-back as a matter of routine. And when he's making it, there's nothing any defender in the world can do about it. 
110.2The Lakers' 110.2 defensive rating with Dončić on the court would register as a top-10 mark. For all the talk about Dončić's poor defense, he hasn't been nearly as bad with the Lakers as he was with the Mavericks (especially in the 2024 Finals, the clips from which are going to haunt him forever), and he's been downright good so far this season. It's early, yes, and individual defensive stats can be deceiving, but nonetheless Dončić is tied for sixth league-wide with 15 steals (he's been a genuine ball hawk early), and he's tied for the league lead in charges with four. And get this: Opponents are shooting just 32.3 percent so far with Dončić as their defender, which is the best mark in the league among all players who are defending at least 12 shots per game. Better than Victor Wembanyama! 

        
            
                Luka Dončić explains his 'step forward' on defense after five-steal performance vs. Raptors
                
                    Robby Kalland                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Again, these can be deceiving markers. Dončić obviously isn't an elite defender, and that opponent shooting percentage is going to vary wildly on Dončić simply being the closest defender on misses rather than the one genuinely forcing someone into a bad shot. Also, he's defending perimeter shots, so on some level, shooters are just missing a lot of shots with him nearby so far. But the 3-pointers are the ones where he's just the guy closing out a lot (which is still important). Inside the arc, you're much more responsible for effecting misses, and have a look at this entering the Portland game. 
Bottom line, a 110.2 defensive rating with Dončić on the floor is what it is. At the very least, he hasn't been a liability, which, given his offensive production, is a major win. 
130.9The Lakers' offensive rating with Dončić on the floor this season, which would be an NBA record. When he isn't on the floor, the offense falls to a 99.1 rating, which would rank as the worst in the league by a long shot. As Austin Reaves is finding out in the non-Luka minutes, life is mighty difficult without one of the greatest offensive players in history out there to command all the attention and still break defenses down like a cardboard box. 203Including Friday night, the Lakers have won Dončić's on-floor minutes this season by a total of 140 points and lost his bench minutes by 63. Do the math, and he has single-handedly represented a 203-point swing so far. If you are looking for one MVP number, this might be it.

title: 2026 NFL trade deadline targets: Ranking top 25 players who could be traded - CBS Sports
description: Saquon Barkley, Jonathan Taylor, Kirk Cousins and more could fetch returns at the trade deadline
body:
Saquon Barkley, Jonathan Taylor, Kirk Cousins and more could fetch returns at the trade deadline
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:22 am ET
                        
                •
            
            9 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The NFL trade deadline is less than two weeks away. That means the hot stove will heat up considerably fairly soon. We've already seen multiple high-profile deals this season, with Joey Porter Jr. heading to the Cowboys, Marvin Harrison Jr. heading to the Texans, Quenton Nelson heading to the Seahawks, DeForest Bucker landing with the 49ers and Jeffery Simmons being traded to the Bears, and we could see several more in the coming days, given how wide open the league appears to be at the moment. With that in mind, we wanted to take a look at some of the top targets who could be on the move. We ranked the top situations that bear the most watching, but with a twist. Some of them are team-wide, meaning there are multiple targets that interested teams could pursue over the next two weeks. There are 25 targets in all. (The Nelson, Buckner and Simmons deals make us 3-for-3 on predicting players that could be dealt, from the original list below. The list has since been updated.)So without further ado, here's the list...The Eagles 
Saquon Barkley's contract, with all the various option bonuses included, makes dealing with him somewhat financially complicated, but given the Eagles' struggles, his age, and the fact that teams are looking for explosiveness at running back these days, he makes sense as a target for needy teams. His current injury situation muddies the picture a bit, but that could be cleared up in the coming days and weeks as he gets further away from the hamstring pull.Moro Ojomo is in the final year of his rookie contract. The Eagles just paid big money to two defensive tackles (Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis), so they probably can't afford to keep Ojomo around. He's 25 years old and has shown production upside with 6 sacks last season.  
If the Eagles want to get aggressive, they can consider dealing both him and Nolan Smith, whose fifth-year option they picked up for next season but who they probably can't afford to keep in the longer term. Smith is more of a force in the run game than as a pass rusher, but that could still be valuable for teams that need help on the edge. Dallas Goedert, meanwhile, signed a renegotiated contract with the Eagles this past offseason and is carrying only a $1.3 million base salary. He's not the most dynamic tight end these days, but he's a reliable pass-catcher and blocker, and any team that needs an additional tight end (teams love multi-tight end sets these days) could get interested for a small price. The Colts 
Nelson is already on the move, traded to the Seahawks for a pair of draft picks. Bucker is gone, too, having been sent back to the 49ers after seven years away.
Jonathan Taylor is one of the best running backs in the NFL and has been able to remain productive even while the Colts' offense has fallen apart around him. (He's only at 4.2 yards per carry, but he's carrying a 55% rushing success rate, per Pro-Football-Reference.) He's the type of explosive back who can change an offense in the way Kenneth Walker III did for the Chiefs. The contract isn't prohibitive for trade purposes, as the Colts would incur only $10 million in dead money next year if they move him. DeForest Buckner has also been traded away. Josh Downs has reportedly requested a trade away from Indianapolis, and with the wide receiver in the final year of his rookie contract, the Colts should seriously consider moving him if they're not going to give him a new deal this offseason. He hasn't been particularly productive this year due to Daniel Jones' struggles, but he's been a per-route star in prior years, so he could help a team in need of receiver depth.The Titans 
Simmons has already been dealt, heading to the Bears for two first-rounders and more. 
Amani Hooker is a very good, very versatile safety (he's played 232 snaps in the box, 127 as a deep safety and 56 as a slot corner so far this year), and those are valuable around the NFL. He still has three years left on his contract, including 2026, so there is a team-control aspect that would be valuable to a potentially acquiring team. Tony Pollard is in the final year of his deal with only a $6.7 million base salary. He's 29 years old, but if you look under the hood, the numbers show he's actually running pretty well so far this season. He's 10th in yards after contact per attempt among the 39 running backs with 50-plus carries, for example, according to Tru Media. He's also 12th in explosive run rate. He can still play, and help a team in need of a committee back. Calvin Ridley has completely fallen out of favor in Tennessee and could potentially help a team in need of depth-chart wide receiver help. 
The Chargers 
Khalil Mack is on a one-year deal with an $8 million base salary. He's got three sacks in six games and has played 71% of the Chargers' defensive snaps. He's not going to be the player he once was, but any team in need of a rotational pass rusher should give the Chargers a call to see if they can get him for a late pick. Tuli Tuipulotu only has two sacks in the Chargers' six games, but a deeper look at the numbers reveals a player playing better than that. He's 23rd in pressure rate among 148 players with 100 or more pass-rush snaps, according to Tru Media, and 18th in havoc play rate. He's still just 24 years old and you can get out ahead of his free agency by acquiring him now. Derwin James, like Jeffery Simmons, recently signed a contract extension, so it would be somewhat surprising to see him get dealt. But he's 31 years old, the Chargers are terrible, and he's one of their most valuable assets. His base salaries for the next three years are also pretty high ($17.5 million, $24.6 million and $21.5 million), so the return might not be as much as the Chargers would be looking for. 
Quentin Johnston only has 8 catches for 165 scoreless yards this season, and he's seemingly been surpassed in the target pecking order. He also has an $18 million salary for next season after the Chargers picked up his fifth-year option. So the return is likely to be low, but it's hard to imagine that L.A. wants to keep him around. Donte Jackson is in the final year of his deal with only a $6 million base salary. He could be of help to any team in need of a cornerback, and there are always teams that need help in the defensive backfield. If the Chargers actually decide to sell, he seems like one of the more likely candidates to move.The Cardinals 
Budda Baker has base salaries of $14.4 million and $16.1 million this year and next, but he's a valuable enough player to make those price tags worth it. He's extremely versatile and can play both the run and the pass, whether lined up deep or in the box. He's 30 years old and still likely has several quality seasons left under his belt. The Cardinals aren't going to contend for the postseason, and Baker is their best asset for future value.  
Josh Sweat is having a down year, both sack-wise (2 in 7 games) and in terms of his pressure rate (7.9%). And his contract doesn't exactly make that type of production attractive. But his track record over the long term, up to and including last year, is much more impressive, and teams could bet that he has a bounce-back in a more favorable environment. He probably wants a new contract, but that could be worked out once you see him play for your team. The Dolphins 
Win over the Jets notwithstanding, the Dolphins look like arguably the worst team in the league this season. Zach Sieler, though, remains a quality player. He hasn't been at his best this season (nobody on the Dolphins has), but we've seen high upside as both a run defender and a pass rusher from the defensive interior. If you can tap back into that, his base salaries over the next few years are very affordable ($44.5 million from 2027 through 2029, none of which is guaranteed). Jordyn Brooks, like Jeffery Simmons and Derwin James, recently signed an extension. But his deal actually made him easier to trade and gave the Dolphins the benefit of selling to an acquiring team, knowing they'd have Brooks under team control for multiple years. With the emergence of rookie Jacob Rodriguez and Brooks having recently turned 29 years old, they could look to deal him for a pretty sizable return. 
Brian Thomas Jr.  
Brian Thomas Jr. has pretty clearly fallen out of favor in Jacksonville. In the Jaguars' last game, he didn't play a single second-half snap. Rookie Josh Cameron is playing ahead of him, and now it seems that two-way star Travis Hunter might be as well. But Thomas has more of a track record of high-level production than did Marvin Harrison Jr., and MHJ fetched a second-round pick via trade. If the Jaguars could get that type of return, they should be very interested, and teams should be interested in acquiring him as well, considering what he did as a rookie (albeit maybe not for quite that high a price, considering what he's done this year and last).Daron Payne 
The Commanders are going nowhere and Daron Payne is in the final year of his contract. His $16.4 million base salary is high but not prohibitive to a trade. He's still a quality run defender, even if he doesn't give you that much in the way of pass-rush juice these days. The Commies would be wise to get something for him before he leaves in free agency next offseason. Will McDonald IV 
Will McDonald IV has seen his snap rate cut from 66% down to 46% this season after the arrival of David Bailey in the draft. But he had 10.5 and 8 sacks over the last two seasons, and has shown he can be a productive pass rusher. The Jets just lost to the aforementioned Dolphins, so it's not like they're really going to compete for anything this year. McDonald had his fifth-year option picked up for next season, but he's still affordable. 
Kirk Cousins 
Klint Kubiak is already getting questions about when he's going to turn the reins over to Fernando Mendoza, which means Kirk Cousins' time under center is likely coming to an end fairly soon. Like Brissett, he could be valuable to a team looking for either a quality backup or a fill-in starter for the rest of the season. The Raiders might prefer to just keep him around and have him mentor Mendoza for the rest of the year, though. Jauan Jennings
Jauan Jennings has so far been entirely uninvolved in the Vikings' offense. It would be surprising to see the league's last remanining unbeaten team make a trade where the give away an asset instead of acquire one, but given Jennings' lack of role and the number of teams in need of wide receiver help, this is certainly a situation worth monitoring.Yaya Diaby
It might be surprising to see the Buccaneers sell given the state of the AFC South, but Diaby is one of the players it might make sense to move, given his contract situation and what the Bucs have elsewhere at the position. Diaby is in the final year of his rookie-scale contract and is probably not going to get paid by the Bucs this offseason given the emergence of David Walker and the fact that they just drafted Rueben Bain Jr. If Tampa loses to the Falcons and/or Bears in these next couple weeks, he could make it to the trade block.

title: Bret Bielema jokes Illinois would 'probably be a top-15 team' if Illini were in the SEC after getting to 6-3 - CBS Sports
description: Bielema's Illini have won four straight and he couldn't help jabbing at the CFP's love for the SEC
body:
Bielema's Illini have won four straight and he couldn't help jabbing at the CFP's love for the SEC
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:24 am ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Bret Bielema's Illinois squad got off to a disastrous start to the season, opening the year 2-3 with one of the nation's worst defenses. After losing to Purdue at home, it seemed the Illini might be in for a long year in the Big Ten's basement, but a defensive coordinator change and a well-timed bye week have seen Illinois go on a four-game winning streak. After beating Nebraska 24-13 on Friday night, Illinois is riding a four-game winning streak and is bowl-eligible again at 6-3. Bielema and his staff have done an incredible job getting a defense that was giving up north of 34 points per game through the first six weeks dialed back in after the bye, allowing 13.3 points per game in their last three wins. That improvement had Bielema sticking his chest out a bit on Friday night and taking a crack at the first batch of College Football Playoff Rankings that showed an awful lot of love to the SEC. "I think about as we're building things here at Illinois, now we're three seasons in a row that we'll have postseason play, which is absolutely awesome and really hard for anybody," Bielema said, via ESPN. "... If we were in the SEC, we'd probably be a top-15 team. We've just got to continue to stay on track where we're at and do a really good job of holding the moment and putting ourselves in a position to be successful."
While top 15 is being facetious, a few three-loss teams have cracked the top 25 -- No. 21 South Carolina, No. 23 Oregon and No. 24 Florida. Bielema noted that while the Illini are thrilled to get to bowl eligibility, their dreams of crashing the playoff aren't completely dead. Depending on what happens the rest of the way in a fascinating Week 10 slate, several other teams could join that group at three losses, and with the carnage we've seen around the country, it seems like a lock that by the end of the year there are a couple of three-loss squads sniffing around the top 12. The Illini are unlikely to be among the teams given serious consideration with three losses, but if they've rattled off seven straight wins that include Oregon, UCLA and Iowa (the latter two being their next two opponents), Bielema would have a real case for Illinois being deserving of consideration at the least. 
A playoff berth this season may be far-fetched, but the Illini will be one of the teams likely to benefit from the expansion to 24 teams in 2027. Bielema has built that program into a perennial threat to finish in the top 25, and once the field doubles, Illinois will have a great opportunity to make its first appearance in the dance.

title: Frustrated Derrick Henry responds to trade rumors, Ravens not expected to deal him, per report - CBS Sports
description: Henry was not a happy camper after Baltimore's fourth straight setback
body:
Henry was not a happy camper after Baltimore's fourth straight setback
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:48 am ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        After a 4-1 start, the Baltimore Ravens have now lost four straight following Thursday night's lopsided loss to the visiting Jacksonville Jaguars. The Ravens' current plight raised questions about Derrick Henry's future in Baltimore ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline.A clearly frustrated Henry fielded questions after Thursday night's loss, and he gave a candid response when directly asked about his future with the Ravens. "I'm not mentioning me going anywhere else," he said. "I'm saying let's go back to work, try to get better and turn this around."The stance on a potential Henry trade is not exclusive to the running back himself. According to ESPN, the Ravens are not expected to trade him during the season, and the front office informed him that it has no intentions of doing so. There has reportedly never been any consideration of a deal.
At this point, Henry remains focused on doing what he can to help the Ravens turn their season around. But while his mindset is admirable, there's not much Henry can do to help fix Baltimore's current issues. Even if Jacoby Brissett plays well, it's going to be hard for the Ravens to make up ground in the AFC North. Baltimore is currently last in the division; they trail the first-place Steelers by 2.5 games. The Ravens are currently three spots out of the AFC's final wild-card spot. When you add in Lamar Jackson's uncertain future with the team, it might make sense for Baltimore to begin rebuilding now rather than delay the inevitable. 

        
            
                Why Ravens should trade Derrick Henry: Don't let Baltimore's QB woes drag down 'King Henry'
                
                    Bryan DeArdo                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
There would have been no shortage of offers if the Ravens decided to trade Henry, who on Thursday night moved into seventh on the NFL's career rushing list. The Vikings, Giants, Patriots, and Packers are among the NFL's playoff-contending teams that could use help at the running back position. Henry would have figured to command significant compensation on the trade market if the Ravens entertained any offers. While his age — he'll be 33 by the end of the regular season — is a factor that could have hurt his trade value, it would have only taken one team to drive up the price.A championship is essentially the only thing that has eluded Henry to this point in his career, and a trade might have expedited his search for a Super Bowl. Instead, it looks as though he will have to wait at least another year as the Ravens fall out of contention.

title: Cowboys should consider trading George Pickens: 5 logical destinations at NFL trade deadline - CBS Sports

body:
Pickens received only four targets in Dallas' historic collapse against Arizona, adding urgency to the Cowboys' decision before the NFL trade deadline
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:21 am ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        ARLINGTON, Texas -- Shortly after Chad Ryland's game-winning field goal went through the uprights to seal a 33-30 comeback, Dallas Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens flew down the hallway and into the locker room by himself. No other teammate, coach, or staff member moved faster to get into the locker room and out of AT&T Stadium after Dallas made ugly history with its blown 14-point lead.
Pickens' lack of targets was glaring. CeeDee Lamb led the way with 11 targets on Sunday while tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford was second with five targets. Pickens caught two passes for 48 yards. Four targets in a game simply isn't enough.Pickens hasn't been bad this season: his 533 yards receiving rank as the 15th most in the NFL in 2026, just behind Trey McBride and just in front of Garrett Wilson (527) and Ja'Marr Chase (492). He is still on pace to exceed 1,100 receiving yards, but it regularly feels like the Cowboys are leaving production out on the field. Since Schottenheimer blamed Pickens' lack of vigor for run blocking for the team's struggling offense in a loss to the Green Bay Packers, he has 10 targets across the last two games. "If I had the answer, we'd get him involved. I'm not trying to be rude or whatever it is, but he made some plays. Anytime the ball went his way, he came up with them. He had the one, unfortunately came back for a holding," quarterback Dak Prescott said. ... "I'm not sure about even how many targets he had. As I told y'all before, I go through the reads. [I] try to throw it to the open guy and stay consistent and true to that. And so, I've got to go back and look at the film and see if I missed him, see if we could have went to him more, see if we could have went to CeeDee more. I feel like it was a game that CeeDee didn't have as many catches as per usual, but we still had a chance to win and should have won it."
With the NFL trade deadline coming up in eight days on Nov. 10 and the Cowboys off to a 3-5 start and appearing to be going nowhere, it would make sense for Dallas to field trade calls for Pickens. He is playing out the franchise tag, and he will command near-top-of-the-market value on his second multi-year NFL contract. Dallas will also have to deal with balancing cornerback Joey Porter Jr.'s contract situation, since he, too, is set to be a free agent after the season. After trading away draft capital to get Porter Jr. and Quinnen Williams, Dallas could use some additional ammunition in its 2027 NFL Draft war chest. So who could be blowing up owner/general manager Jerry Jones' phone for Pickens if word leaks out that they will listen to trade calls for their 25-year-old Pro Bowl wideout? Here is a look at five potential landing spots. Landing spots
                            
    
                                                
                    
    San Francisco 49ersRecord: 6-1Jerry Jones has shown he doesn't care about sending a young star player to a non-divisional rival: he traded Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers. The pairing of the 49ers and Pickens makes too much sense.
San Francisco is the NFC's top seed through the first eight weeks of the season, and they have $34.98 million in cap space, the third most in the entire league, per OverTheCap.com. There are no financial barriers to this deal. Plus, they have a glaring need for Pickens given all their wide receiver injuries. Both Mike Evans (ribs, Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) were ruled out of their last game played in Week 7. Three wide receivers are on their injured reserve list.Lastly, the 49ers are all in for 2026 because of their aging core. Christian McCaffrey is 30, Evans is 33, Samuel is 30, George Kittle is 33, Kyle Juszcyk is 35, Trent Williams is 38 and DeForest Buckner is 32. Both Fred Warner and Nick Bosa are healthy right now, but they're both 29 with extensive injury histories. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Kansas City ChiefsRecord: 5-2The Chiefs failed to score a game-winning touchdown after having a second-and-goal at the one with 15 seconds left, and Kansas City was outscored 15-0 in the fourth quarter of their narrow 28-24 road loss against the Denver Broncos on Sunday. You know who could have made a significant difference for quarterback Patrick Mahomes in the fourth quarter in Week 8? The 6-foot-3, 200-pound Pickens.Kenneth Walker III is starting to lose a little steam after being heavily relied upon to carry the Chiefs' offense on his back. After averaging 133 rushing yards per game and 6.3 yards per carry with six rushing touchdowns in Kansas City's first five games of the season, Walker III is now averaging 52.5 rushing yards per game and 3.0 yards per carry without a touchdown in the last two games. That's because the Chiefs' passing game requires Travis Kelce to be their No. 1 target, something that isn't a sustainable formula over the course of an 18-week season and beyond. Also, it would be incredibly foolish to waste the rest of Mahomes' glory years. The three-time Super Bowl MVP quarterback is 31, but he hasn't been the same high-flying passer that he was with a true No. 1 wide receiver like Tyreek Hill. Without Hill since 2022, Mahomes' production has taken a notable dip.

    Buffalo Bills Record: 6-1  The Buffalo Bills are the AFC's No. 1 seed through the first eight weeks, and they are always in win-now mode with Josh Allen. Yes, the Bills traded for DJ Moore, but he is probably best as Buffalo's No. 2 receiver on a Super Bowl team. He missed Buffalo's last two games with a shoulder injury prior to returning in Week 8, and he hyperextended his knee in the Bills' 36-10 beatdown of the Lamar Jackson-less Ravens.Allen hasn't had a true WR1 since the 2024 Stefon Diggs trade. Pickens could help him become the league's most efficient passer. That would probably be enough for the Bills to perhaps win their first Super Bowl in franchise history. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Las Vegas RaidersRecord: 4-4The Las Vegas Raiders trading for Pickens would be a case of taking care of the now and the later. The Kirk Cousins-led Raiders are 4-4 and just one game out of the AFC's No. 7 seed. Giving Cousins, whose 19 passing touchdowns rank as the second most in the NFL, Pickens to pair with Brock Bowers could really make Klint Kubiak's offense pop. Among the players officially listed as wide receivers on the Raiders' roster, Tre Tucker, a 2023 third-round pick, is the best they have. He could also help accelerate Fernando Mendoza's long-term development. Pickens is just two years older than the 23-year-old Mendoza, so the quarterback could spend the bulk of his career with a high-caliber wide receiver in addition to the 23-year-old Bowers at tight end. Perhaps living in Las Vegas would dull the novelty of going out on The Strip that Pickens and Lamb experienced when they visited for "Monday Night Football" last season. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Minnesota VikingsRecord: 6-1Despite being 6-1 and the No. 2 seed in the NFC, the Minnesota Vikings have the sixth-lowest scoring offense (20.0 points per game) in the entire NFL. Their lack of rhythm in the passing game is a major reason for that, as their Kyler Murray-quarterbacked passing attack is averaging the second-fewest passing yards per game (165.6) in the entire NFL.Yes, Minnesota has 2022 NFL Offensive Player of the Year Justin Jefferson and former first-round pick Jordan Addison at wide receiver, but its offense could clearly use another weapon to help Murray find his groove as a Viking. They have been rumored to be in pursuit of Jonathan Taylor, but perhaps Pickens could also help fix the issues on the offensive side of the ball.

title: Chargers not interested in Khalil Mack trade, will retain top offensive players despite 0-7 record, per report - CBS Sports
description: The winless Chargers will stick to the status quo
body:
The winless Chargers will stick to the status quo
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 7, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:35 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The only winless team in the NFL may stand firm at the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Despite their deeply disappointing start to the season, the Los Angeles Chargers reportedly have no interest in moving their perceived top trade candidates. According to ESPN, the front office made it clear to other teams that edge rusher Khalil Mack will remain a Charger at the deadline, and any questions regarding quarterback Justin Herbert and wide receiver Ladd McConkey were met with "hard nos."If the Chargers were to make a deal by Tuesday, Mack would be perhaps the least surprising trade piece considering he is on an expiring contract and continues to play disruptive football from the edge rusher position, which is always in demand. But Los Angeles has always been steadfast in its desire to keep the future Hall of Famer in town through the end of his deal. Mid-round draft capital would be a reasonable return for the 35-year-old, but instead the Chargers repeatedly shut down outside interest in one of their top defensive assets."I want Khalil Mack here," coach Jim Harbaugh said this week. "Khalil Mack wants to be here. He's one of the pillars of our team."It is less surprising that Los Angeles put a fence around Herbert and McConkey since they could remain building blocks for whatever kind of rebuild the franchise undertakes. Herbert remains under team control through 2029, and McConkey's rookie deal runs through the end of next season. When the offense is non-dysfunctional, they are standout players.
The obvious issue, however, is that the offense is dysfunctional this season. Herbert threw more interceptions (10) than any other quarterback in the NFL over the first eight weeks, and his 69.3 passer rating is second-worst only to Daniel Jones among qualifying signal-callers. McConkey is on pace for his least productive season as a pro with only 17 catches across six games.Moving on from those offensive weapons would likely require the Chargers to sell low, because the offense's overall woes have cast a shadow over both players. That appears to be a non-starter.Chargers stick to status quo despite putrid recordThe Chargers reportedly do not like the message of giving up on this season. But at 0-7 and with more of their losses coming by more than one possession than not, the hole they dug themselves into over the first two months of the campaign is deeper than that of any other team. There is very little to play for the rest of the way.
Los Angeles is opposed to trading its most valuable tools, but by holding onto them, it is declining to cash in on the potential draft picks it would receive in return. For a team that is clearly not equipped to contend in the near future, rebuilding through the draft would be a logical step forward. Instead, it will keep intact a core that has not won a playoff game in the Harbaugh era.Player personnel is not the only part of this operation that remains unchanged, either. Harbaugh retained offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel through the bye week, which also came as a surprise since his system is the least productive in the NFL. No team averages fewer points per game than the Chargers at 14.1. The only tangible change to the offense has come in the form of McDaniel moving from the sideline to the box for Week 9.If the definition of insanity is doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results, then the Chargers -- by way of keeping their roster intact and declining to make changes on the coaching staff -- fit that bill.
